To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified novel breast cancer subgroups by integrating DNA and RNA data from 2,000 patients, which have distinct clinical outcome and are associated with specific gene expression networks.
we have integrated DNA and RNA data in breast cancer and identified subgroups with distinct genomic, transcriptomic and clinical features.

1) we performed the first comprehensive integrated analysis of copy-number variation and gene expression in primary breast tumours; 2) we identified new breast cancer subgroups with distinct survival outcome; 3) we identified novel putative cancer genes and cancer gene networks; and 4) we identified new molecular mechanisms underlying cancer subtypes, such as the adaptive immune response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterisation of the genetic and molecular subtypes of breast cancer, and their clinical relevance.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of breast cancer, which will lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets and biomarkers for breast cancer.
the elucidation of breast tumour biology and stratification through integration of the genomic and transcriptomic profiles of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors have provided a comprehensive analysis of the genomic landscape of breast cancer and its impact on the transcriptome, which has revealed novel subgroups of patients that may have important clinical utility.
this study has provided a novel molecular stratified view of the breast cancer landscape, based on the integration of copy number and transcriptome.

this paper presents an integrated analysis of the genomic and transcriptomic landscape of 2,002 breast tumours, revealing novel subtypes and the impact of somatically acquired copy number aberrations on gene expression and gene networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large scale genomic and transcriptomic analysis of breast tumours has identified novel subgroups with different prognoses.
we have integrated DNA copy number data and transcriptomic data in order to identify subtypes of breast cancer.
the genomic and transcriptomic landscape of breast cancer can be used to define new subgroups of breast cancer with prognostic and predictive value, and to define the underlying biology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genomic landscape of breast cancer is dominated by copy number alterations (CNAs) which have major effects on gene expression.

the landscape of somatic CNVs and their effects on the transcriptome are much more extensive than previously appreciated and that the effects are often trans acting, i.e. not limited to the genomic region of the CNV itself.
the integration of copy number and expression data can provide a more accurate and clinically relevant classification of breast cancer.
